meaning_en: Disturbing and horrifying because it is concerned with death or injury.
meaning_es: Perturbador y horripilante por estar relacionado con la muerte o el daño.
note: Often used approvingly of dark humour or art that confronts mortality unflinchingly, not merely as a criticism.

examples.en: The museum's macabre collection of Victorian death masks drew curious visitors.
examples.es: La macabra colección de máscaras mortuorias victorianas del museo atraía a visitantes curiosos.

examples.en: She had a macabre sense of humour that her colleagues either loved or found deeply uncomfortable.
examples.es: Tenía un sentido del humor macabro que a sus compañeros o les encantaba o les resultaba profundamente incómodo.

meaning_en: Generous or forgiving, especially toward a rival or someone less powerful.
meaning_es: Generoso o comprensivo, especialmente con un rival o con alguien de menor poder.
note: Implies moral greatness, not just kindness; typically used when someone chooses grace over advantage.

examples.en: He was magnanimous in defeat, congratulating his opponent warmly in front of the cameras.
examples.es: Fue magnánimo en la derrota y felicitó a su contrincante con calidez ante las cámaras.

examples.en: The magnanimous offer to share the prize money surprised everyone who knew her.
examples.es: La magnánima oferta de compartir el premio sorprendió a todos los que la conocían.

meaning_en: Ineffective or clumsy, particularly in social situations or handling problems.
meaning_es: Torpe o poco hábil, especialmente en situaciones sociales o al resolver problemas.
note: Suggests a lack of social or practical skill; slightly more damning than 'clumsy' because it implies poor judgment.

examples.en: His maladroit attempt to defuse the argument only made things worse.
examples.es: Su torpe intento de calmar la discusión no hizo más que empeorar las cosas.

examples.en: The minister's maladroit comments on live television triggered an immediate backlash.
examples.es: Los desafortunados comentarios del ministro en televisión en directo desencadenaron una reacción inmediata.

meaning_en: Having or showing a desire to harm others; wishing ill on others.
meaning_es: Que tiene o muestra deseo de hacer daño a los demás; que les desea el mal.
note: Suggests a deep-seated ill will, often used of characters in fiction or when describing deliberate, targeted intent.

examples.en: The character's malevolent grin left the audience in no doubt about his intentions.
examples.es: La sonrisa malévola del personaje no dejó al público ninguna duda sobre sus intenciones.

examples.en: She described the campaign as a malevolent attempt to destroy his reputation.
examples.es: Describió la campaña como un intento malintencionado de destruir su reputación.

meaning_en: Easily shaped, influenced, or persuaded; adaptable to new circumstances.
meaning_es: Fácilmente moldeable, influenciable o persuadible; adaptable a nuevas circunstancias.
note: Can be neutral (adaptable) or mildly critical (easily manipulated) depending on context.

examples.en: Young voters tend to be more malleable in their political opinions than older generations.
examples.es: Los votantes jóvenes suelen tener opiniones políticas más maleables que las generaciones anteriores.

examples.en: The new manager found the team malleable enough to adopt the revised workflow quickly.
examples.es: El nuevo gerente encontró al equipo lo suficientemente flexible como para adoptar el nuevo flujo de trabajo rápidamente.

meaning_en: Clear and obvious to the eye or mind; unmistakable.
meaning_es: Evidente y obvio para los ojos o la mente; inequívoco.
note: Used where something is so evident it would be hard to dispute; carries a formal, legalistic weight beyond 'obvious'.

examples.en: The tribunal found manifest errors in the way the evidence had been assessed.
examples.es: El tribunal detectó errores manifiestos en la forma en que se había valorado la prueba.

examples.en: Her relief at the verdict was manifest; she broke into tears before the judge had finished speaking.
examples.es: Su alivio ante el veredicto era manifiesto; rompió a llorar antes de que el juez terminara de hablar.

meaning_en: Sentimental in an exaggerated or feeble way; sickeningly sweet.
meaning_es: Sentimental de forma exagerada o empalagosa; dulzón hasta el exceso.
note: Used critically; implies the emotion is performed rather than genuinely felt, or so excessive it becomes off-putting.

examples.en: The film's mawkish ending undermined two hours of otherwise restrained storytelling.
examples.es: El empalagoso final de la película echó por tierra dos horas de narración por lo demás contenida.

examples.en: He avoided the mawkish tributes and instead shared a funny anecdote about his mentor.
examples.es: Evitó los sentimentales homenajes y en su lugar compartió una anécdota graciosa sobre su mentor.

meaning_en: A deep, pensive sadness; a prolonged feeling of low spirits.
meaning_es: Una tristeza profunda y pensativa; un estado prolongado de ánimo decaído.
note: Often carries a reflective or even pleasurable connotation in literary use, unlike depression, which is clinical.

examples.en: Autumn always brought with it a quiet melancholy she couldn't quite explain.
examples.es: El otoño siempre traía consigo una callada melancolía que ella no sabía bien cómo explicar.

examples.en: The song was saturated with a melancholy that made it impossible to listen to without feeling something.
examples.es: La canción estaba impregnada de una melancolía que hacía imposible escucharla sin sentir algo.

meaning_en: Not telling the truth; dishonest in what one says or writes.
meaning_es: Que no dice la verdad; deshonesto en lo que dice o escribe.
note: A formal word for deliberate dishonesty; can describe a single misleading claim as readily as a pattern of behaviour.

examples.en: The report described the official's testimony as mendacious and self-serving.
examples.es: El informe calificó el testimonio del funcionario de mendaz e interesado.

examples.en: She was tired of his mendacious excuses and stopped asking for explanations altogether.
examples.es: Estaba harta de sus mentirosas excusas y dejó de pedir explicaciones por completo.

meaning_en: Subject to sudden, unpredictable changes of mood or mind.
meaning_es: Sujeto a cambios de humor o de opinión repentinos e impredecibles.
note: Can be admiring (brilliant but unpredictable) or cautionary; the context usually clarifies which sense is intended.

examples.en: His mercurial nature made him an exciting collaborator but a difficult long-term partner.
examples.es: Su naturaleza mercurial lo convertía en un colaborador apasionante pero en un socio difícil a largo plazo.

examples.en: The team never quite knew what to expect from their mercurial coach.
examples.es: El equipo nunca sabía muy bien qué esperar de su imprevisible entrenador.

meaning_en: Showing great attention to detail; very careful and precise.
meaning_es: Que presta gran atención al detalle; muy cuidadoso y preciso.
note: Generally positive; describes thorough, careful work. Can edge toward critical when implying excessive caution.

examples.en: The restorer's meticulous work brought the sixteenth-century painting back to life.
examples.es: El meticuloso trabajo del restaurador devolvió la vida al cuadro del siglo XVI.

examples.en: She kept meticulous records of every transaction, which proved invaluable during the audit.
examples.es: Llevaba un registro meticuloso de cada transacción, lo que resultó de gran valor durante la auditoría.

meaning_en: Expressing or conveying a threat; menacing in tone or manner.
meaning_es: Que expresa o transmite una amenaza; de tono o actitud amenazante.
note: Rarer than 'threatening' or 'menacing'; used to highlight a deliberate, often official or legal, air of intimidation.

examples.en: The letter's minatory tone left no room for doubt that legal action would follow.
examples.es: El tono amenazante de la carta no dejaba lugar a dudas de que se tomarían acciones legales.

examples.en: He gave her a minatory look that silenced any further questions.
examples.es: Le lanzó una mirada amenazante que silenció cualquier pregunta adicional.

meaning_en: Make less severe, serious, or painful; lessen the harmful effects of something.
meaning_es: Hacer algo menos grave, serio o doloroso; reducir los efectos perjudiciales de algo.
note: Widely used in law, policy, and risk management. 'Mitigate against' is a common usage error; the verb takes a direct object.

examples.en: Better insulation can significantly mitigate heat loss in older buildings.
examples.es: Un mejor aislamiento puede reducir significativamente las pérdidas de calor en los edificios más antiguos.

examples.en: The judge accepted that his cooperation had mitigated his role in the scheme.
examples.es: El juez aceptó que su cooperación había atenuado su papel en el plan.

meaning_en: Appease or placate someone who is angry or distressed; soften in feeling.
meaning_es: Apaciguar o calmar a alguien que está enojado o angustiado; suavizar los ánimos.
note: Implies active effort to calm; the word suggests the person doing the calming takes the grievance seriously.

examples.en: An apology and a refund did little to mollify the passengers whose flights had been cancelled.
examples.es: Una disculpa y un reembolso hicieron poco por calmar a los pasajeros cuyos vuelos habían sido cancelados.

examples.en: She tried to mollify her colleague with coffee and a carefully worded explanation.
examples.es: Intentó apaciguar a su colega con un café y una explicación cuidadosamente formulada.

meaning_en: Sharply critical or sarcastic with a biting, often dark quality.
meaning_es: Mordaz o sarcástico, con una agudeza hiriente y a menudo oscura.
note: Overlaps with 'acerbic'; mordant often has a darker, bleaker edge and tends to describe humour as much as criticism.

examples.en: His mordant commentary on corporate life made the column compulsive reading.
examples.es: Su mordaz comentario sobre la vida corporativa convertía la columna en una lectura obligada.

examples.en: The playwright's mordant wit turned a domestic dispute into a comedy of genuine cruelty.
examples.es: El ingenio mordaz del dramaturgo convirtió una disputa doméstica en una comedia de auténtica crueldad.

meaning_en: In a dying state; lacking vitality and likely to come to an end soon.
meaning_es: En estado de agonía; sin vitalidad y con pocas probabilidades de sobrevivir.
note: Used both literally and figuratively; in non-literal use, it implies not just decline but near-inevitable end.

examples.en: The once-thriving high street had become moribund, with more empty units than open shops.
examples.es: La otrora animada calle comercial se había quedado moribunda, con más locales vacíos que tiendas abiertas.

examples.en: Critics wrote the genre off as moribund, but sales figures told a different story.
examples.es: Los críticos daban al género por muerto, pero las cifras de ventas decían otra cosa.

meaning_en: Sullen, ill-tempered, and silent; unhappy without communicating why.
meaning_es: Hosco, malhumorado y silencioso; abatido sin exteriorizar el motivo.
note: Combines sadness with withdrawal and an unwillingness to engage; the sullenness itself is the defining quality.

examples.en: He sat morose and unresponsive at the end of the table throughout the entire dinner.
examples.es: Estuvo sentado durante toda la cena en el extremo de la mesa, hosco y sin abrir la boca.

examples.en: A week of grey weather had left even the most cheerful staff members feeling morose.
examples.es: Una semana de cielo gris había dejado incluso al personal más animado sumido en un estado de mal humor.

meaning_en: Having many varied parts, elements, or aspects; highly diverse.
meaning_es: Que tiene muchas partes, elementos o aspectos variados; muy diverso.
note: Often used to suggest productive variety rather than confusion; implies richness rather than disorder.

examples.en: The role demands a person capable of juggling multifarious responsibilities without losing focus.
examples.es: El puesto requiere a alguien capaz de gestionar múltiples y variadas responsabilidades sin perder el foco.

examples.en: The festival celebrated the multifarious cultural traditions of the city's residents.
examples.es: El festival celebraba las múltiples y variadas tradiciones culturales de los habitantes de la ciudad.

meaning_en: More generous than is usual or expected; lavishly open-handed.
meaning_es: Más generoso de lo habitual o esperado; espléndido y dadivoso.
note: Implies abundance in giving; the scale of the generosity is what distinguishes it from ordinary generosity.

examples.en: The family's munificent endowment funded the university's new arts centre.
examples.es: La munificente donación de la familia financió el nuevo centro de artes de la universidad.

examples.en: She accepted the munificent offer with surprise, having expected a far smaller settlement.
examples.es: Aceptó la generosa oferta con sorpresa, pues había esperado un acuerdo mucho menor.

meaning_en: Liable or subject to change; not fixed or permanent.
meaning_es: Sujeto o propenso al cambio; no fijo ni permanente.
note: More formal and neutral than 'changeable'; often used in philosophy, biology, or policy contexts.

examples.en: Public opinion on the issue proved surprisingly mutable over the course of the trial.
examples.es: La opinión pública sobre el asunto resultó ser sorprendentemente variable durante el transcurso del juicio.

examples.en: The organisation's structure is mutable and designed to adapt as the project evolves.
examples.es: La estructura de la organización es mutable y está diseñada para adaptarse a medida que el proyecto evoluciona.

meaning_en: Unclear, vague, or loosely defined; lacking a clear form or outline.
meaning_es: Impreciso, vago o mal definido; sin una forma o contorno claro.
note: Often implies the vagueness is a problem; more critical than 'abstract', suggesting the idea can't be pinned down usefully.

examples.en: The proposal was full of nebulous promises but short on specific commitments.
examples.es: La propuesta estaba llena de promesas vagas pero escasa de compromisos concretos.

examples.en: Her career plan remained nebulous, more a feeling than an actual strategy.
examples.es: Su plan de carrera seguía siendo nebuloso, más una sensación que una estrategia real.

meaning_en: Wicked, criminal, or deeply dishonest.
meaning_es: Malvado, criminal o profundamente deshonesto.
note: Carries a theatrical quality; often used with a hint of irony as well as genuine criticism of wrongdoing.

examples.en: The investigation uncovered the nefarious dealings of a network of shell companies.
examples.es: La investigación descubrió las turbias actividades de una red de empresas pantalla.

examples.en: He joked that his weekend plans were entirely nefarious, raising more laughs than eyebrows.
examples.es: Bromeó diciendo que sus planes para el fin de semana eran absolutamente nefastos, arrancando más carcajadas que ceños fruncidos.

meaning_en: Failing to give proper care or attention; careless about one's duty.
meaning_es: Que no presta la debida atención o cuidado; descuidado en el cumplimiento de sus obligaciones.
note: Has a legal sense (breach of duty of care) as well as a general one; context usually signals which is intended.

examples.en: The contractor was found negligent for failing to inspect the scaffolding before work began.
examples.es: El contratista fue declarado negligente por no inspeccionar el andamio antes de que comenzaran los trabajos.

examples.en: It would be negligent not to mention the study's significant methodological limitations.
examples.es: Sería negligente no mencionar las importantes limitaciones metodológicas del estudio.

meaning_en: Appearing casually unconcerned; relaxed and indifferent in a studied or natural way.
meaning_es: Aparentemente despreocupado; relajado e indiferente, ya sea de forma natural o estudiada.
note: Can describe either genuine ease or a performance of ease; tone and context clarify whether it's authentic or affected.

examples.en: She gave a nonchalant wave and walked off as if nothing had happened.
examples.es: Hizo un gesto despreocupado con la mano y se marchó como si no hubiera pasado nada.

examples.en: His nonchalant attitude during the interview suggested he was already confident he'd got the job.
examples.es: Su actitud despreocupada durante la entrevista sugería que ya estaba convencido de que había conseguido el trabajo.

meaning_en: The state of being famous for something bad or scandalous.
meaning_es: El estado de ser famoso por algo malo o escandaloso.
note: The fame is for something undesirable; the word carries a negative charge that 'fame' does not. 'Notorious' is the adjective.

examples.en: The case brought the defendant unwanted notoriety that followed him for years.
examples.es: El caso le trajo al acusado una notoriedad no deseada que lo persiguió durante años.

examples.en: The neighbourhood had gained notoriety as a flashpoint for late-night disturbances.
examples.es: El barrio se había ganado mala fama como punto conflictivo de altercados nocturnos.

meaning_en: Characterised by subtle distinctions; not simple or clear-cut.
meaning_es: Caracterizado por matices sutiles; no simple ni tajante.
note: Often praise in intellectual contexts; can be used dismissively when 'nuanced' means the speaker won't take a clear position.

examples.en: The documentary offered a nuanced portrait of the conflict, resisting the urge to assign blame.
examples.es: El documental ofrecía un retrato matizado del conflicto y resistía la tentación de atribuir culpas.

examples.en: Her nuanced reading of the policy revealed contradictions that a casual observer would have missed.
examples.es: Su lectura matizada de la política reveló contradicciones que un observador superficial habría pasado por alto.

meaning_en: Stubbornly refusing to change one's opinion or course of action.
meaning_es: Que se niega obstinadamente a cambiar de opinión o de actuación.
note: Implies a deliberate hardening of position, not just stubbornness; often used in political or negotiating contexts.

examples.en: The council remained obdurate in the face of protests, refusing to reconsider the planning decision.
examples.es: El ayuntamiento se mantuvo inflexible ante las protestas y se negó a reconsiderar la decisión urbanística.

examples.en: Her obdurate refusal to compromise ultimately cost her the negotiation.
examples.es: Su obstinada negativa a ceder le costó finalmente la negociación.

meaning_en: Excessively eager to serve or please; fawning to the point of insincerity.
meaning_es: Excesivamente servicial o adulador; zalamero hasta la falta de sinceridad.
note: The eagerness to please is so excessive that it reads as insincere or cringing rather than genuine deference.

examples.en: The waiter's obsequious manner made the guests feel less like diners and more like targets.
examples.es: Los modales obsequiosos del camarero hacían que los comensales se sintieran más como objetivos que como clientes.

examples.en: She had little patience for the obsequious tone that junior staff adopted around the new director.
examples.es: Le faltaba paciencia para el tono servil que el personal júnior adoptaba en presencia del nuevo director.

meaning_en: Noisy and hard to control; unruly in a loud and disruptive way.
meaning_es: Ruidoso y difícil de controlar; alborotador de forma escandalosa y perturbadora.
note: The noise is central; it's not just defiant but loudly so. Often used with mild exasperation rather than serious condemnation.

examples.en: The obstreperous children at the next table made conversation almost impossible.
examples.es: Los ruidosos niños de la mesa de al lado hacían casi imposible mantener una conversación.

examples.en: A handful of obstreperous protesters interrupted the press conference three times.
examples.es: Un puñado de manifestantes alborotadores interrumpió la rueda de prensa en tres ocasiones.

meaning_en: Annoyingly slow to understand; stupidly unperceptive.
meaning_es: Irritantemente torpe para comprender; que no capta las cosas.
note: Can suggest genuine dimness or wilful refusal to understand; 'deliberately obtuse' implies the latter.

examples.en: She repeated the instruction slowly, wondering whether he was being obtuse or simply distracted.
examples.es: Repitió la instrucción despacio, preguntándose si él estaba siendo obtuso o simplemente estaba distraído.

examples.en: The reviewer's deliberately obtuse questions seemed designed to embarrass rather than to inform.
examples.es: Las preguntas deliberadamente torpes del crítico parecían pensadas para avergonzar más que para informar.

meaning_en: Asserting authority or offering unsolicited advice in an intrusive, domineering way.
meaning_es: Que ejerce la autoridad o da consejos no solicitados de forma intrusiva y dominante.
note: Note the spelling: officious ≠ official. The word criticises petty overreach, not authority in itself.

examples.en: An officious security guard insisted on checking everyone's bag a second time.
examples.es: Un guardia de seguridad excesivamente celoso insistió en revisar el bolso de todos por segunda vez.

examples.en: She found the officious tone of the letter unnecessary given how minor the issue was.
examples.es: El tono autoritario de la carta le pareció innecesario teniendo en cuenta lo insignificante del asunto.

meaning_en: Giving the impression that something bad or unpleasant is about to happen.
meaning_es: Que da la impresión de que algo malo o desagradable está a punto de ocurrir.
note: Used both literally of weather or atmosphere and figuratively of social or political signals; well-established in all registers.

examples.en: The ominous silence from headquarters suggested the announcement would not be good news.
examples.es: El ominoso silencio de la sede central sugería que el comunicado no sería buena noticia.

examples.en: Dark clouds gathered overhead, casting an ominous shadow over the outdoor ceremony.
examples.es: Las nubes oscuras se fueron acumulando sobre sus cabezas, proyectando una sombra inquietante sobre la ceremonia al aire libre.

meaning_en: Involving great effort or difficulty; burdensome and hard to fulfil.
meaning_es: Que implica un gran esfuerzo o dificultad; oneroso y difícil de cumplir.
note: Common in legal and contractual language to describe obligations whose cost or effort is excessive relative to the benefit.

examples.en: The new compliance rules placed onerous reporting demands on small businesses.
examples.es: Las nuevas normas de cumplimiento imponían a las pequeñas empresas exigencias de información muy gravosas.

examples.en: He found the paperwork onerous but accepted it as part of the job.
examples.es: Encontraba el papeleo muy pesado pero lo aceptaba como parte del trabajo.

meaning_en: Not transparent; difficult to understand or interpret clearly.
meaning_es: Que no es transparente; difícil de comprender o interpretar con claridad.
note: Often a criticism of deliberate obscurity; in policy or finance, opaque systems hide accountability or risk.

examples.en: The contract's language was so opaque that even the lawyers struggled to parse it.
examples.es: El lenguaje del contrato era tan opaco que hasta los abogados tenían dificultades para interpretarlo.

examples.en: The committee's decision-making process remained opaque despite calls for greater transparency.
examples.es: El proceso de toma de decisiones del comité siguió siendo opaco a pesar de los llamamientos a una mayor transparencia.

meaning_en: Appearing to be true or real but possibly not; stated or seeming to be the case.
meaning_es: Que parece verdadero o real pero que quizás no lo es; que se declara o aparenta ser así.
note: The word signals scepticism; the speaker implies a hidden reality beneath the stated surface.

examples.en: The ostensible aim of the visit was goodwill; its real purpose was gathering intelligence.
examples.es: El objetivo aparente de la visita era promover la buena voluntad; su propósito real era recabar información.

examples.en: He accepted the ostensible explanation while quietly doubting its accuracy.
examples.es: Aceptó la explicación aparente mientras dudaba en silencio de su veracidad.

meaning_en: Designed to impress or attract notice; showy in a way that suggests a lack of taste.
meaning_es: Diseñado para impresionar o llamar la atención; llamativo de un modo que sugiere falta de gusto.
note: Used critically; the issue is the intent to attract notice rather than any inherent quality of the thing.

examples.en: The house was lavishly furnished in a style that bordered on the ostentatious.
examples.es: La casa estaba lujosamente decorada con un estilo que rozaba la ostentación.

examples.en: His ostentatious generosity at charity events seemed calculated to win attention.
examples.es: Su ostentosa generosidad en los actos benéficos parecía calculada para atraer la atención.

meaning_en: In a state of excessive agitation or nervous tension; too distressed to think or act calmly.
meaning_es: En un estado de agitación o tensión nerviosa excesiva; demasiado alterado para pensar o actuar con calma.
note: Describes a state of heightened distress, usually following a stressful event or piece of news.

examples.en: By the time the results came in, she was so overwrought that she could barely speak.
examples.es: Para cuando llegaron los resultados, estaba tan alterada que apenas podía hablar.

examples.en: She arrived overwrought, convinced something had gone wrong with the flight booking.
examples.es: Llegó muy alterada, convencida de que algo había salido mal con la reserva del vuelo.

meaning_en: So intense or obvious as to seem almost tangible; plain to see or feel.
meaning_es: Tan intenso u obvio que parece casi tangible; claramente visible o perceptible.
note: Often used to describe atmosphere or emotion; it adds vividness by suggesting the feeling can almost be physically touched.

examples.en: The tension in the room was palpable as the votes were counted.
examples.es: La tensión en la sala era palpable mientras se contaban los votos.

examples.en: When the rescuers emerged safely, the crowd's relief was palpable.
examples.es: Cuando los rescatadores emergieron sanos y salvos, el alivio de la multitud era palpable.

meaning_en: Small or meagre in a way that is contemptibly inadequate.
meaning_es: Escaso o insuficiente de manera despreciable.
note: The contempt is built-in; it expresses not just smallness but the speaker's low opinion of whether the amount is appropriate.

examples.en: After two years of work, the bonus she received felt like a paltry acknowledgement.
examples.es: Después de dos años de trabajo, el bono que recibió le pareció un reconocimiento ridículo.

examples.en: The company donated a paltry amount compared with the profits it had made that quarter.
examples.es: La empresa donó una cantidad irrisoria comparada con los beneficios que había obtenido ese trimestre.

meaning_en: Extremely unwilling to spend money or use resources; excessively frugal.
meaning_es: Extremadamente reacio a gastar dinero o recursos; excesivamente frugal.
note: More formal and critical than 'frugal'; the implication is that the restraint has passed the point of reasonable caution.

examples.en: The parsimonious budget allocated to training left staff demoralised and underprepared.
examples.es: El escaso presupuesto destinado a la formación dejó al personal desmoralizado e insuficientemente preparado.

examples.en: She was parsimonious with praise, believing that giving it too freely would devalue it.
examples.es: Era tacaña con los elogios, convencida de que prodigarlos demasiado los devalúa.

meaning_en: Excessively concerned with minor rules, details, or formalism; overly literal.
meaning_es: Excesivamente preocupado por normas menores, detalles o formalismos; demasiado literal.
note: Used critically; the person may be technically correct but is prioritising rules over what actually matters in context.

examples.en: It may seem pedantic, but the difference between 'less' and 'fewer' has a practical function.
examples.es: Puede parecer pedante, pero la diferencia entre 'less' y 'fewer' tiene una función práctica.

examples.en: The pedantic debate over the heading format delayed the entire report by three days.
examples.es: El debate pedante sobre el formato del encabezado retrasó todo el informe tres días.

meaning_en: Expressing contempt or disapproval; conveying a low or negative opinion.
meaning_es: Que expresa desprecio o desaprobación; que transmite una opinión baja o negativa.
note: Most often used to describe words or language rather than general attitudes; it is descriptive, not itself an insult.

examples.en: He used the word in its pejorative sense, leaving no doubt that he meant it as a slight.
examples.es: Empleó la palabra en su acepción peyorativa, sin dejar ninguna duda de que pretendía ser un insulto.

examples.en: The term has shifted over decades and is no longer primarily pejorative.
examples.es: El término ha evolucionado a lo largo de las décadas y ya no es principalmente peyorativo.

meaning_en: Engaged in deep or serious thought, often with a tinge of sadness.
meaning_es: Absorto en pensamientos profundos o serios, a menudo con cierto matiz de tristeza.
note: The sadness is implied rather than certain; it describes inward-focused thought rather than active deliberation.

examples.en: She stood at the window in a pensive silence, gazing out at the garden.
examples.es: Se quedó de pie junto a la ventana en un silencio pensativo, mirando el jardín.

examples.en: The photograph caught him in a pensive moment, chin resting on his hand.
examples.es: La fotografía lo captó en un momento de ensimismamiento, con la barbilla apoyada en la mano.

meaning_en: Insisting on immediate compliance; brusque and not allowing for discussion.
meaning_es: Que exige obediencia inmediata; brusco y que no admite discusión.
note: Carries authority plus impatience; implies the speaker sees no need to justify themselves or entertain objections.

examples.en: His peremptory dismissal of the proposal angered the team, who felt they hadn't been heard.
examples.es: Su brusco rechazo de la propuesta enfadó al equipo, que sintió que no había sido escuchado.

examples.en: She received a peremptory message ordering her to report to the head office that afternoon.
examples.es: Recibió un mensaje perentorio ordenándole que se presentara en la sede central esa misma tarde.

meaning_en: Carried out with minimal effort or care; done as routine with little thought.
meaning_es: Realizado con el mínimo esfuerzo o atención; hecho por rutina y sin mucha reflexión.
note: The problem is indifference, not incompetence; the task is completed but without engagement or care.

examples.en: He gave the safety checklist a perfunctory glance before signing it without reading it.
examples.es: Le echó un vistazo superficial a la lista de verificación de seguridad antes de firmarla sin leerla.

examples.en: The apology was so perfunctory that it felt more like an insult than an attempt to repair things.
examples.es: La disculpa fue tan superficial que pareció más un insulto que un intento de reparar las cosas.

meaning_en: Having a harmful effect, especially in a gradual or subtle way.
meaning_es: Que tiene un efecto dañino, especialmente de forma gradual o sutil.
note: Often used of influences, habits, or beliefs whose damage is cumulative and not immediately obvious.

examples.en: The pernicious myth that talent alone determines success discourages effort and perseverance.
examples.es: El pernicioso mito de que el talento por sí solo determina el éxito desalienta el esfuerzo y la perseverancia.

examples.en: Doctors warned about the pernicious long-term effects of chronic sleep deprivation.
examples.es: Los médicos advirtieron de los perniciosos efectos a largo plazo de la privación crónica de sueño.

meaning_en: Having a ready insight into things; shrewd and perceptive.
meaning_es: Que tiene una gran capacidad de intuición; sagaz y perspicaz.
note: Implies more than intelligence; it suggests a quality of noticing what others miss, often in human or social situations.

examples.en: A perspicacious reader will spot the clues scattered through the novel's opening chapter.
examples.es: Un lector perspicaz detectará las pistas diseminadas por el capítulo inicial de la novela.

examples.en: Her perspicacious assessment of the market proved correct when the sector reversed six months later.
examples.es: Su perspicaz valoración del mercado resultó acertada cuando el sector dio un giro seis meses después.

meaning_en: Childishly sulky or ill-tempered; irritable in a way that seems immature.
meaning_es: Malhumorado o susceptible de forma infantil; irritable de un modo que parece inmaduro.
note: Describes a reaction that seems disproportionate or childishly irritable; makes no claim about whether the feeling is justified.

examples.en: He responded to the criticism with a petulant tweet that did little for his reputation.
examples.es: Respondió a la crítica con un tuit irritable que no hizo ningún bien a su reputación.

examples.en: Her petulant refusal to discuss the matter made negotiations much harder than they needed to be.
examples.es: Su irritable negativa a discutir el asunto hizo las negociaciones mucho más difíciles de lo necesario.

meaning_en: Calm and unemotional; not easily excited or disturbed.
meaning_es: Tranquilo y sereno; que no se agita ni se altera con facilidad.
note: Now used neutrally or admiringly for steady composure under pressure; the historical humour-theory sense is not in play.

examples.en: He remained phlegmatic throughout the crisis, calmly issuing instructions as others panicked.
examples.es: Permaneció impasible durante toda la crisis, dando instrucciones con calma mientras los demás se desesperaban.

examples.en: Her phlegmatic response to the news surprised those who had expected a more dramatic reaction.
examples.es: Su flemática reacción ante la noticia sorprendió a quienes habían esperado una reacción más dramática.

meaning_en: Seeming reasonable or probable; having an appearance of truth or credibility.
meaning_es: Que parece razonable o probable; que tiene apariencia de verdad o credibilidad.
note: Importantly, plausible does not mean true; it describes what seems credible, leaving open whether it actually is.

examples.en: She offered a plausible excuse for her absence, though no one entirely believed it.
examples.es: Ofreció una excusa plausible para su ausencia, aunque nadie la creyó del todo.

examples.en: The theory sounds plausible on the surface, but the data do not support it.
examples.es: La teoría parece plausible en la superficie, pero los datos no la respaldan.

meaning_en: Easily influenced or persuaded; yielding readily without strong resistance.
meaning_es: Fácilmente influenciable o persuadible; que cede con facilidad sin ofrecer gran resistencia.
note: Mildly negative when applied to people; suggests a lack of independent judgement or will.

examples.en: The new regime sought a pliant media that would report without challenge.
examples.es: El nuevo régimen buscaba unos medios de comunicación dóciles que informaran sin cuestionar nada.

examples.en: She was far less pliant than her predecessor, frequently pushing back on board decisions.
examples.es: Era mucho menos dócil que su predecesora y con frecuencia se oponía a las decisiones de la junta.

meaning_en: Evoking a keen sense of sadness or regret, often through something beautiful or tender.
meaning_es: Que evoca un profundo sentido de tristeza o nostalgia, a menudo a través de algo bello o delicado.
note: Describes something that produces a sharp emotional response, typically sadness or nostalgia, often mixed with beauty or tenderness.

examples.en: The old photographs were poignant reminders of a friendship that illness had eventually severed.
examples.es: Las viejas fotografías eran conmovedores recordatorios de una amistad que la enfermedad había acabado truncando.

examples.en: There was something poignant about watching the last train leave the station before it closed.
examples.es: Había algo conmovedor en ver salir el último tren de la estación antes de que cerrara.

meaning_en: Affectedly grand or self-important; speaking or behaving as if one is more important than one is.
meaning_es: Afectadamente grandilocuente o engreído; que habla o actúa como si fuera más importante de lo que es.
note: Used critically; the pompous person is not merely formal but inflated with a self-importance that others find overblown.

examples.en: The pompous preamble to the memo stretched to three paragraphs before reaching its single point.
examples.es: El pomposo preámbulo del memorando se extendió durante tres párrafos antes de llegar a su único punto.

examples.en: He could be charming in small groups but became pompous on stage, as if performing a character.
examples.es: Podía ser encantador en grupos pequeños, pero se volvía pomposo en el escenario, como si interpretara a un personaje.

meaning_en: Dealing with things in a practical way rather than according to fixed theories or principles.
meaning_es: Que aborda las cosas de manera práctica en lugar de seguir teorías o principios fijos.
note: Generally positive in everyday use; implies getting things done over abstract debates. Can be used critically when it signals opportunism.

examples.en: The pragmatic decision to accept a smaller deal was criticised by those who wanted to hold out.
examples.es: La pragmática decisión de aceptar un acuerdo menor fue criticada por quienes querían esperar a algo mejor.

examples.en: She took a pragmatic view of the situation, focusing on what could actually be changed.
examples.es: Adoptó una visión pragmática de la situación, centrándose en lo que realmente podía cambiarse.

meaning_en: Done or acting with undue haste; rash and without careful consideration.
meaning_es: Hecho o actuado con precipitación excesiva; impulsivo y sin la debida reflexión.
note: As an adjective, means hasty and reckless; as a verb, means to cause something to happen suddenly.

examples.en: The precipitate withdrawal of funding caused the project to collapse before completion.
examples.es: La precipitada retirada de la financiación provocó el colapso del proyecto antes de su finalización.

examples.en: He later admitted that the sale had been precipitate and he had accepted far too low a price.
examples.es: Más tarde admitió que la venta había sido precipitada y que había aceptado un precio demasiado bajo.

meaning_en: A strong preference or liking for something; a particular fondness.
meaning_es: Una preferencia o gusto marcado por algo; una afición especial.
note: Neutral in tone; does not imply the preference is excessive, merely that it is pronounced and consistent.

examples.en: His predilection for understatement made his rare moments of emphasis all the more powerful.
examples.es: Su predilección por la sobriedad hacía que sus escasos momentos de énfasis resultaran aún más poderosos.

examples.en: The director has a well-known predilection for long, uninterrupted takes.
examples.es: El director tiene una conocida predilección por los planos largos e ininterrumpidos.

meaning_en: Having knowledge of events before they happen; showing accurate foresight.
meaning_es: Que conoce los hechos antes de que ocurran; que muestra una previsión certera.
note: Typically used retrospectively, once events have confirmed the person's foresight to be accurate.

examples.en: The economist's prescient warnings about systemic risk went largely unheeded before the crash.
examples.es: Las proféticas advertencias de la economista sobre el riesgo sistémico fueron ignoradas en gran medida antes de la crisis.

examples.en: Looking back, the novel seems prescient in its depiction of a surveillance society.
examples.es: En retrospectiva, la novela parece premonitoria en su descripción de una sociedad de vigilancia.

meaning_en: Claiming greater importance, merit, or distinction than is justified.
meaning_es: Que pretende una importancia, mérito o distinción mayor de la que está justificada.
note: Used critically; the person or thing claims a status it cannot back up, and the gap is what strikes observers.

examples.en: The menu's pretentious descriptions made simple dishes sound like feats of culinary philosophy.
examples.es: Las pretenciosas descripciones del menú hacían que los platos sencillos sonaran como hazañas de filosofía culinaria.

examples.en: He found the gallery's artist statements pretentious, full of jargon and empty of meaning.
examples.es: Encontraba las notas de los artistas de la galería pretenciosas, llenas de jerga y vacías de significado.

meaning_en: To avoid stating the truth directly; to speak or act evasively.
meaning_es: Evitar decir la verdad directamente; hablar o actuar de manera evasiva.
note: Describes deliberate evasion or obfuscation; the speaker avoids giving a direct answer through vagueness or misdirection.

examples.en: He prevaricated for several minutes before the interviewer pressed him to give a direct answer.
examples.es: Estuvo dando rodeos durante varios minutos hasta que el entrevistador lo presionó para que respondiera directamente.

examples.en: Stop prevaricating and tell me whether you intend to sign the contract or not.
examples.es: Deja de andarte con rodeos y dime si tienes intención de firmar el contrato o no.

meaning_en: Remarkably great in extent, size, or degree; impressively large or extensive.
meaning_es: Extraordinariamente grande en magnitud, tamaño o grado; impresionantemente vasto.
note: Generally positive; the scale is so great it provokes admiration. Can carry mild irony when used of appetite or excess.

examples.en: She had a prodigious memory, able to recall conversations verbatim years after they had taken place.
examples.es: Tenía una memoria prodigiosa y era capaz de recordar conversaciones al pie de la letra años después de haberlas tenido.

examples.en: The team put in a prodigious amount of work to meet the deadline.
examples.es: El equipo realizó una cantidad prodigiosa de trabajo para cumplir el plazo.

meaning_en: Recklessly extravagant or wasteful, especially with money or resources.
meaning_es: Despilfarro o derrochador de forma irresponsable, especialmente con el dinero o los recursos.
note: Emphasises reckless excess; the word focuses on the scale of the waste rather than the person's attitude toward it.

examples.en: Critics accused the administration of profligate spending that had ballooned the national debt.
examples.es: Los críticos acusaron a la administración de un gasto pródigo que había disparado la deuda nacional.

examples.en: His profligate lifestyle in his twenties left him in serious financial difficulty by thirty-five.
examples.es: Su vida derrochadora a los veinte años lo dejó en graves dificultades económicas a los treinta y cinco.

meaning_en: Producing a large quantity of work, offspring, or results.
meaning_es: Que produce gran cantidad de obras, descendencia o resultados.
note: Describes volume, not quality; a prolific writer may or may not be a good one. Usually admiring but neutral in meaning.

examples.en: She was a prolific letter writer, sending detailed correspondence to dozens of friends each week.
examples.es: Era una escritora de cartas prolífica y enviaba correspondencia detallada a docenas de amigos cada semana.

examples.en: The striker was the most prolific scorer in the league's history, with 312 career goals.
examples.es: El delantero fue el máximo goleador de la historia de la liga, con 312 goles en su carrera.

meaning_en: Using too many words; tediously lengthy or wordy.
meaning_es: Que utiliza demasiadas palabras; prolijo y tediosamente extenso.
note: A criticism of writing or speech; implies the wordiness dilutes rather than develops the message.

examples.en: The professor's prolix lecture notes tested the patience of even the most dedicated students.
examples.es: Los prolijos apuntes del profesor pusieron a prueba la paciencia incluso de los estudiantes más dedicados.

examples.en: The contract was so prolix that key clauses were buried in pages of irrelevant padding.
examples.es: El contrato era tan prolijo que las cláusulas clave estaban enterradas en páginas de relleno irrelevante.

meaning_en: Giving or indicating a good chance of success; favourably disposed.
meaning_es: Que augura o indica buenas perspectivas de éxito; favorablemente dispuesto.
note: More formal than 'favourable'; often describes timing or circumstance rather than a person's intentions.

examples.en: The economic climate was not propitious for launching an expensive product.
examples.es: El clima económico no era propicio para lanzar un producto caro.

examples.en: She waited for a more propitious moment to raise the issue with her manager.
examples.es: Esperó un momento más propicio para plantearle el asunto a su jefa.

meaning_en: Lacking imagination or originality; dull and ordinary.
meaning_es: Sin imaginación ni originalidad; aburrido y ordinario.
note: Implies something that could have been interesting or elevated is flat and unimaginative instead.

examples.en: The truth, as it turned out, was far more prosaic than the rumours had suggested.
examples.es: La verdad, según resultó, era mucho más prosaica de lo que los rumores habían dado a entender.

examples.en: She gave a prosaic account of the accident, listing facts without any narrative shape.
examples.es: Dio un relato prosaico del accidente, enumerando hechos sin darle ninguna forma narrativa.

meaning_en: Having a narrow, unsophisticated outlook associated with life away from major centres.
meaning_es: Con una visión estrecha y poco sofisticada asociada a la vida alejada de los grandes centros urbanos.
note: Can describe geography or mentality; applied to people, it is a criticism of limited perspective and resistance to new ideas.

examples.en: Her provincial assumptions about city life turned out to be comically inaccurate.
examples.es: Sus prejuicios provincianos sobre la vida en la ciudad resultaron ser cómicamente erróneos.

examples.en: The committee's provincial outlook made it slow to respond to changes in the wider industry.
examples.es: La mentalidad provinciana del comité lo hacía lento para responder a los cambios en el sector en general.

meaning_en: Acting with care and thought for the future; sensible and avoiding unnecessary risk.
meaning_es: Que actúa con cuidado y pensando en el futuro; sensato y que evita riesgos innecesarios.
note: Positive in most contexts; suggests mature, forward-thinking restraint rather than timidity.

examples.en: It was prudent to get a second opinion before committing to the surgery.
examples.es: Era prudente pedir una segunda opinión antes de comprometerse con la cirugía.

examples.en: The prudent investor had diversified her portfolio years before the market turned.
examples.es: La prudente inversora había diversificado su cartera años antes de que el mercado cambiara.

meaning_en: Eager or quick to argue, quarrel, or fight; combative in manner.
meaning_es: Dispuesto o propenso a discutir, pelear o confrontar; de carácter pendenciero.
note: Can be mildly admiring of someone who fights their corner effectively, or critical of someone who picks fights needlessly.

examples.en: His pugnacious cross-examination style unsettled the witness more than the questions themselves did.
examples.es: Su estilo combativo en el contrainterrogatorio desestabilizó al testigo más que las propias preguntas.

examples.en: She was pugnacious by nature, never willing to let a slight pass without responding.
examples.es: Era combativa por naturaleza y nunca dejaba pasar un agravio sin responder.

meaning_en: Complaining in a petulant, irritable, or whining manner.
meaning_es: Que se queja de forma quejumbrosa, irritable o lastimera.
note: Describes a complaining or whining tone; can colour a single question or remark as much as a sustained disposition.

examples.en: Her querulous tone throughout the meeting made it difficult to take her concerns seriously.
examples.es: Su tono quejumbroso durante toda la reunión dificultó que sus preocupaciones fueran tomadas en serio.

examples.en: He grew querulous in old age, complaining about everything from the weather to the neighbours.
examples.es: Con la vejez se volvió quejumbroso y se lamentaba de todo, desde el tiempo hasta los vecinos.

meaning_en: Exceedingly idealistic and unrealistic; pursuing noble but impractical goals.
meaning_es: Excesivamente idealista e irrealista; que persigue objetivos nobles pero poco prácticos.
note: From Don Quixote; implies admirable but futile idealism. Often used with a mix of affection and mild exasperation.

examples.en: His quixotic plan to reform the tax code single-handedly earned him respect but no results.
examples.es: Su quijotesco plan para reformar el código fiscal en solitario le granjeó respeto pero ningún resultado.

examples.en: It was a quixotic undertaking, and everyone knew it, but she pursued it regardless.
examples.es: Era una empresa quijotesca y todo el mundo lo sabía, pero ella la emprendió de todas formas.

meaning_en: Of or occurring every day; belonging to ordinary, everyday experience.
meaning_es: Que ocurre o se da cada día; propio de la experiencia cotidiana y ordinaria.
note: Often used to elevate the mundane or to highlight its contrast with something exceptional.

examples.en: The novel finds beauty in the quotidian rituals of a family's morning routine.
examples.es: La novela encuentra belleza en los rituales cotidianos de la rutina matutina de una familia.

examples.en: Her job involved the quotidian drudgery of data entry, relieved only by the occasional interesting project.
examples.es: Su trabajo implicaba la tediosa rutina cotidiana de la introducción de datos, aliviada solo por algún proyecto interesante ocasional.

meaning_en: Bitter, long-lasting resentment or ill feeling toward someone.
meaning_es: Rencor amargo y duradero hacia alguien.
note: British spelling; US English uses 'rancor'. The feeling is persistent and deep-seated, not a momentary reaction.

examples.en: Years after the dispute, he still spoke of his former partner with unconcealed rancour.
examples.es: Años después de la disputa, seguía hablando de su exsocio con un rencor no disimulado.

examples.en: She managed to end the relationship without rancour, which impressed everyone who had witnessed the fallout.
examples.es: Logró poner fin a la relación sin rencor, lo que impresionó a todos los que habían presenciado la ruptura.

meaning_en: To cause continuing annoyance, irritation, or resentment.
meaning_es: Causar una irritación, molestia o rencor persistentes.
note: Describes a grievance that persists quietly over time; the irritation is slow-burning rather than explosive.

examples.en: The decision to pass him over for promotion still rankled years later.
examples.es: La decisión de no ascenderle seguía escociéndole años después.

examples.en: What rankled most was not the decision itself but the way it had been communicated.
examples.es: Lo que más le molestaba no era la decisión en sí, sino la manera en que había sido comunicada.

meaning_en: Aggressively greedy; pursuing money or material gain at the expense of others.
meaning_es: Vorazmente codicioso; que busca dinero o beneficio material a expensas de los demás.
note: Implies predatory or exploitative behaviour; the greed is aggressive, not merely excessive.

examples.en: The rapacious landlord raised rents every six months, forcing out long-term residents.
examples.es: El rapaz casero subía los alquileres cada seis meses, expulsando a los inquilinos de larga data.

examples.en: Critics condemned the rapacious acquisition strategy that swallowed up smaller competitors.
examples.es: Los críticos condenaron la rapaz estrategia de adquisición que engullía a los competidores más pequeños.

meaning_en: Making or characterised by a harsh, loud noise; boisterously rowdy.
meaning_es: Que produce o se caracteriza por un ruido fuerte y estridente; ruidosamente alborotador.
note: Can be used without disapproval of lively, boisterous scenes; the noise is central to the word's meaning.

examples.en: Raucous laughter from the adjoining room made it impossible to focus on the call.
examples.es: Las ruidosas carcajadas de la habitación de al lado hacían imposible concentrarse en la llamada.

examples.en: The pub was raucous with football supporters celebrating the win.
examples.es: El pub resonaba con el bullicio de los aficionados al fútbol que celebraban la victoria.

meaning_en: Stubbornly uncooperative; resistant to authority or discipline.
meaning_es: Obstinadamente reacio a cooperar; resistente a la autoridad o la disciplina.
note: Describes stubborn resistance to control or compliance; used of people, institutions, or situations that refuse to cooperate.

examples.en: The recalcitrant debtor refused to engage with the court's payment plan for over a year.
examples.es: El recalcitrante deudor se negó a acogerse al plan de pago del tribunal durante más de un año.

examples.en: Dealing with the recalcitrant supplier held up the entire production schedule.
examples.es: Tratar con el proveedor reticente retrasó todo el calendario de producción.

meaning_en: Express disapproval or disappointment to someone because of their behaviour; find fault with.
meaning_es: Expresar desaprobación o decepción a alguien por su comportamiento; censurar.
note: Common in the pattern 'reproach someone for something'. As a noun, 'above/beyond reproach' means impossible to criticise.

examples.en: She reproached herself for not calling him sooner, once she heard how bad things had become.
examples.es: Se reprochó a sí misma no haberle llamado antes, cuando se enteró de lo mal que habían llegado a estar las cosas.

examples.en: His conduct throughout the crisis was beyond reproach, earning respect across party lines.
examples.es: Su conducta durante la crisis fue intachable y le granjeó respeto más allá de las fronteras partidistas.

meaning_en: Not revealing one's thoughts or feelings readily; inclined to say little.
meaning_es: Que no expresa con facilidad sus pensamientos o sentimientos; poco dado a hablar.
note: About communication, not personality; a reticent person may be warm but simply does not share readily.

examples.en: She was reticent about her past, rarely volunteering personal details even to close friends.
examples.es: Era reservada sobre su pasado y rara vez compartía detalles personales incluso con sus amigos íntimos.

examples.en: Both sides remained reticent after the meeting, neither confirming nor denying that talks had broken down.
examples.es: Ambas partes se mantuvieron reservadas tras la reunión, sin confirmar ni desmentir que las conversaciones habían fracasado.

meaning_en: Referring to sexual or bodily matters in a comically direct or irreverent way.
meaning_es: Que alude a asuntos sexuales o corporales de manera cómicamente directa o irreverente.
note: Describes earthy or bawdy humour; the tone is comic rather than malicious, though some audiences may still find it offensive.

examples.en: The play was a ribald comedy that had the audience roaring from start to finish.
examples.es: La obra era una comedia procaz que mantuvo al público riéndose de principio a fin.

examples.en: His ribald anecdotes were a highlight of every gathering, despite the occasional blush they provoked.
examples.es: Sus anécdotas subidas de tono eran el punto álgido de cada reunión, pese a los ocasionales sonrojos que provocaban.

meaning_en: Expressing regret or sorrow, often with a wry or resigned humour.
meaning_es: Que expresa pesar o arrepentimiento, a menudo con un humor socarrón o resignado.
note: Regret mixed with wry self-awareness; the tone is resigned rather than bitter, which sets it apart from simply sorrowful.

examples.en: She gave a rueful smile and admitted she should have taken his advice after all.
examples.es: Esbozó una sonrisa resignada y reconoció que al fin y al cabo debería haber seguido su consejo.

examples.en: Looking back on the episode, he could only shake his head in rueful disbelief.
examples.es: Mirando atrás, solo podía sacudir la cabeza con una incredulidad entre arrepentida y resignada.

meaning_en: Tending to meditate or dwell on thoughts at length; deeply contemplative.
meaning_es: Propenso a meditar o a darle vueltas a los pensamientos durante mucho tiempo; profundamente contemplativo.
note: Implies sustained, inward-turned thinking; often associated with slow, deliberate thinkers or introspective writing.

examples.en: He fell into a ruminative silence that lasted the entire drive home.
examples.es: Cayó en un silencio meditabundo que duró todo el trayecto de vuelta a casa.

examples.en: The ruminative quality of her essays makes them slow reading but deeply rewarding.
examples.es: El carácter meditativo de sus ensayos los hace de lectura lenta pero muy gratificante.

meaning_en: Entangled in or bogged down by a difficult or troublesome situation.
meaning_es: Enredado o atascado en una situación difícil o problemática.
note: Used figuratively to suggest entrapment in a situation; movement is difficult, not just unpleasant.

examples.en: The project became mired in regulatory delays and was eventually abandoned.
examples.es: El proyecto quedó atrapado en retrasos normativos y acabó siendo abandonado.

examples.en: The administration found itself mired in a scandal it could neither contain nor explain away.
examples.es: El gobierno se vio empantanado en un escándalo que no podía contener ni justificar.

meaning_en: Biting or caustic in speech; apt to criticise sharply.
meaning_es: Mordaz o cáustico en el discurso; propenso a criticar con dureza.
note: Rarer than 'mordant'; emphasises the biting quality of criticism rather than its dark or ironic wit.

examples.en: His mordacious reviews made him influential but few subjects agreed to a second interview.
examples.es: Sus mordaces reseñas lo hicieron influyente, pero pocos entrevistados aceptaban una segunda conversación.

examples.en: The mordacious wit of the satirical magazine earned it both admirers and legal threats.
examples.es: El mordaz ingenio de la revista satírica le ganó tanto admiradores como amenazas legales.

meaning_en: Having an excessive interest in death, disease, or disturbing subjects.
meaning_es: Con un interés excesivo por la muerte, la enfermedad o los temas perturbadores.
note: Also a medical term (diseased), but in everyday use it describes someone's preoccupation with gloomy or dark subjects.

examples.en: She had a morbid fascination with true-crime podcasts that she could never quite explain.
examples.es: Sentía una morbosa fascinación por los podcasts de crímenes reales que nunca supo bien cómo explicar.

examples.en: He found it morbid that his colleagues had started placing bets on when the company would fold.
examples.es: Le parecía morboso que sus compañeros hubieran empezado a apostar sobre cuándo cerraría la empresa.

meaning_en: The quality of having strong moral principles; complete honesty and integrity.
meaning_es: La cualidad de tener principios morales sólidos; honradez e integridad completas.
note: High-register praise; used in formal, legal, or political contexts to describe impeccable ethical character.

examples.en: His reputation for probity made him the natural choice to lead the independent inquiry.
examples.es: Su reputación de probidad lo convirtió en la elección natural para presidir la investigación independiente.

examples.en: The profession demanded absolute probity, with any financial impropriety treated as grounds for dismissal.
examples.es: La profesión exigía una probidad absoluta, y cualquier irregularidad económica era motivo de despido.

meaning_en: Lessen the severity of a disease or its symptoms without curing the underlying cause.
meaning_es: Aliviar la gravedad de una enfermedad o sus síntomas sin curar la causa subyacente.
note: In medicine, describes treatment that reduces suffering rather than targeting the root cause; also used figuratively.

examples.en: The treatment could only palliate the pain rather than address its underlying cause.
examples.es: El tratamiento solo podía paliar el dolor en lugar de abordar su causa subyacente.

examples.en: The drug palliates the worst symptoms but does not halt the progression of the disease.
examples.es: El fármaco alivia los peores síntomas, pero no detiene la progresión de la enfermedad.

meaning_en: Spreading widely throughout an area, group, or field of activity.
meaning_es: Que se extiende ampliamente por un área, grupo o campo de actividad.
note: Describes reach, not necessarily force; something pervasive is everywhere, whether noticed or not.

examples.en: The pervasive smell of damp made the building unpleasant regardless of how clean it was kept.
examples.es: El omnipresente olor a humedad hacía que el edificio fuera desagradable independientemente de lo limpio que se mantuviera.

examples.en: A pervasive sense of uncertainty had settled over the market in the weeks before the announcement.
examples.es: Una generalizada sensación de incertidumbre se había apoderado del mercado en las semanas previas al anuncio.

meaning_en: Express sharp, formal disapproval of someone because of their behaviour.
meaning_es: Expresar una desaprobación formal y enérgica de alguien por su comportamiento.
note: Common in the pattern 'rebuke someone for something'; carries more force than a casual criticism and is direct rather than prolonged.

examples.en: The judge rebuked the barrister for interrupting the witness a second time.
examples.es: El juez reprendió al abogado por interrumpir al testigo por segunda vez.

examples.en: The leaked memo was a blunt rebuke of the department's handling of the complaints process.
examples.es: El memorando filtrado era una dura reprimenda por la manera en que el departamento había gestionado el proceso de reclamaciones.

meaning_en: Stubbornly resisting control or treatment; difficult to manage.
meaning_es: Que se resiste obstinadamente al control o al tratamiento; difícil de manejar.
note: Used in medical contexts (a condition that doesn't respond to treatment) as well as general use (a person who won't comply).

examples.en: The condition proved refractory to standard therapy, forcing the team to try an experimental approach.
examples.es: La enfermedad resultó refractaria a la terapia estándar, lo que obligó al equipo a probar un enfoque experimental.

examples.en: The refractory teenager refused all support and had to be allowed to make his own mistakes.
examples.es: El rebelde adolescente rechazó toda ayuda y hubo que permitirle cometer sus propios errores.

meaning_en: Make a protest or objection about something; argue earnestly against an action.
meaning_es: Formular una protesta u objeción sobre algo; argumentar enérgicamente en contra de una acción.
note: Implies a formal or earnest protest rather than a casual complaint; it suggests the speaker believes they have a strong case.

examples.en: She remonstrated with the committee about the decision, citing three procedural irregularities.
examples.es: Protestó ante el comité por la decisión, alegando tres irregularidades de procedimiento.

examples.en: He remonstrated loudly but was outvoted and had no choice but to comply.
examples.es: Protestó con vehemencia, pero fue superado en votos y no tuvo más remedio que acatar la decisión.
